variants.headline: Business plan abandoned before opening
variants.sub: The planned {business} will not open: {founder} has given up the plan.
variants.body:
The founder {founder} has abandoned the plan for {business} before opening. The reason given is that {why}. The builder keeps what it was paid, and any grant is owed back. For {target}, the result raises a direct question about responsibility before an enterprise can begin operating.

Our principles should apply to an unsuccessful beginning as well as a successful one. An abandoned proposal deserves a serious account of obligations, rather than a neat political story about ambition. Public support and private commitment both need a standard that remains visible when a plan does not reach opening.

We criticise {target} on the standard of stewardship. A plan that ends before opening still involves real commitments, and responsibility should not disappear merely because the hoped-for enterprise never began operating. Political principle should remain visible when judgment becomes less comfortable.
